sc-fzoXWK: API Documentation for the AppFolio Reports APIs.

The AppFolio Reports API utilizes REST, allowing you to query and manage data stored in Reports.
We use HTTP Basic Auth for authentication, and application/json to format requests and responses.

sc-fzoXWK: You can execute a previously saved report by its UUID using the GET /saved/{uuid}.json endpoint. This endpoint uses the saved report's stored filters and configuration — no filter parameters are accepted. Pagination parameters (page, limit, paginate_results) work the same as other report endpoints.
sc-fzoXWK (6): Report builder reports are also supported via this endpoint. The same UUID-based lookup applies — open your saved report builder report and copy the UUID from the URL. Report builder reports that combine more than 3 reports are not supported and will return a 422 error. Only columns visible in the UI will be returned. Because report builder reports combine multiple reports, responses may contain duplicate column names. Refer to the response schema of each individual report included in your report builder report to understand the columns that will be returned.

sc-fzoXWK: To prevent network congestion and avoid 429 Too Many Requests errors, we recommend regulating or staggering the rate of your requests. All endpoints have the same rate limits configured, except for the next_page_url, which is not subjected to any rate limits.
sc-fzoXWK (6): Currently, the rate limits are as follows:

sc-fzoXWK: A next page URL value will be returned along with the results of your report when the response contains many rows. The next page URL will contain information about this offset and the existing results of your report run. You can send a POST request directly to this URL to fetch subsequent sets of up to 5,000 rows. We encourage using the next page URL when fetching large sets of data as response times will be considerably faster than generating a new report run. We do not rate limit requests that use this next page URL. Since the next page URL references existing report run results, any changes to filters will not be applied - to avoid confusion here, we do not allow providing filters when using the next page URL in V2.
sc-fzoXWK (6): Next page URLs point to existing results, which are valid for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes you will receive an error message if you attempt to access those results and need to re-run the report with filters to generate new results.
sc-fzoXWK (11): Alternatively, next page URL and the 5,000 row limit can be ignored by providing the flag paginate_results = false. This can result in a lot of data being returned and may take several seconds for the request to complete. You should only use this if it is absolutely necessary and should always include a date range filter to limit the response size. Please note that very long running queries can time out. If you include a paginate_results=false in your request, your response will NOT include the results under a 'results' key - the response payload will just be an array of rows.
